rows.title: A bulleted or numbered list pasted from Word for desktop becomes '·' / '1.' paragraphs, not a list
rows.summary: Now: a list pasted from Word for desktop becomes a real <ul> or <ol>. Word writes each item as a paragraph styled mso-list:lN levelM, with the marker inside <![if !supportLists]> (or the <!--[if !supportLists]--> comment form). Items nest by mso-list level. A numbered marker such as '1.' or 'a)' makes an <ol>. A new list starts when the kind changes, or when the list id changes at level 1. The Symbol, Courier or Wingdings marker, its   padding and the mso-list:Ignore spans are dropped. After review, three more cases work. A paragraph in a Word list style ('List Bullet', 'List Number 2'), whose mso-list is only in the skipped <style> sheet, also becomes a list item; its level comes from the class (MsoListBullet2 gives level 2). An Outlook or Word-HTML list that is already <ol><li style='mso-list:…'> is left as it is, so it stays one numbered list. Before the review fix it was wrapped in a second <ul> and printed as bullets. A marker Word never closed (a cut-off paste) is kept as text and no longer swallows the rest of its paragraph. All of this is in parseRichText (src/utils/richText.js): buildTree keeps the marker in its own #mso-marker node, marked closed at <![endif]>; wordLists() groups p/div/h* items; the walk skips only closed markers. The PDF, the Word and Markdown exports, Design → Lists and the ATS checker all read that one parse. Descriptions saved before the fix, which already start with '·', are not migrated.
rows.product_call: Multi-level legal numbering such as '1.1.' is not read as a number, so that level becomes a bulleted sub-list. The text is kept and only the numbering style differs. A Word heading with list numbering (<h2 style='mso-list:…'>) becomes a numbered item and loses the heading's bold.
rows.remaining: Descriptions stored before the fix keep their literal '·' paragraphs; nothing migrates them. No Playwright spec pastes real Word clipboard HTML in a browser. The fix is checked through sanitizeForInsert and parseRichText in node tests.

notes: One bug was hunted and fixed: c08852d. Its fail-first run, 36562560294, is read from the log: 'fail without the fix (its diff reversed): # fail 2', then 'pass with it'. The review checked stored data: sanitised descriptions carry no mso-list and no conditional comments, so old data parses exactly as before. The review found three regressions or gaps (REV-01 to REV-03) and fixed them in bd23db6 with a fail-first test. CI run 36564399042 ran the review test and the 16 rich-text, ATS and export tests the fixer ran, plus fail-first and lint. The full gate has not run on this branch; it is left for the batch.
